blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Mesolithic Age serves as a transitional phase between the Paleolithic and Neolithic periods.
The era is characterized by the production of microliths—small, refined stone tools attached to bone or wooden handles.
Earliest evidence of animal domestication in India emerges during this period, notably at Bagor and Adamgarh.
Human lifestyle shifted from pure hunting-gathering to semi-sedentary living with fishing and herding.
Prehistoric cave rock art flourished, vividly depicting hunting scenes, dancing, and social life.

blocks.content: The Mesolithic Age represents a critical transition in human history from hunting and gathering toward animal domestication and settled life.

rows: Crude, unpolished large stone tools (hand axes, cleavers)
Hunting, gathering, fishing, and early animal domestication

items: Microliths (1 cm to 8 cm stone tools, often geometric) are uniquely associated with the Mesolithic Age.
Bagor in Rajasthan and Adamgarh in Madhya Pradesh provide the earliest evidence of animal domestication in India.
Bhimbetka rock shelters in Madhya Pradesh contain extensive Mesolithic paintings depicting hunting and social activities.
